SwapSource.description: Where the input tokens come from. Leave unset (or send "WALLET") to pull them from the swapper's wallet as usual. Send "UNIVERSAL_ROUTER" to get calldata that swaps whatever balance of the input token the Universal Router holds when it runs, for bridge-and-swap flows where a bridge deposits into the router and executes the swap in the same transaction. In this mode, quote on the destination chain, use `amount` as your estimate of what will arrive, and put the end user in `swapper`. Exact-input, single-chain swaps only; the returned transaction has no `from` and a `value` of "0". Works on both /quote and /swap. Read the guide before using it: /docs/trading/swapping-api/start-building/integration-guide#swapping-funds-already-in-the-universal-router

EnforceExactIn.description: Only with swapSource "UNIVERSAL_ROUTER". Set it to true when your bridge guarantees how much will arrive; the calldata then checks the router's balance and reverts if it holds less than `amount`. Leave it off if `amount` is just an estimate, or a good fill can revert over a small shortfall. Details: /docs/trading/swapping-api/start-building/integration-guide#swapping-funds-already-in-the-universal-router

MarginDirection.description: Which side of the pair the position is exposed to. `LONG` borrows the counter token and buys the exposure token, so collateral is the exposure token and debt is the counter token. `SHORT` borrows the exposure token and sells it for the counter token, so collateral is the counter token and debt is the exposure token. The market is always addressed in trader terms: a client never sends a collateral/debt pair and never reorders `exposureToken`/`counterToken` to mean short.

MarginDisplay.description:
What the confirmation modal renders: projections of the position IF this action executes. Present state lives on the positions read, not here. Ignored by `POST /plan`: projections are not execution inputs.

Two prices, never mixed: `oraclePrice` is the venue's own mark and drives every risk output, while `effectivePrice` is what the leverage swap realizes and drives sizing. They differ by the spread, and substituting one for the other sizes a position against a figure the swap will not achieve.

A `close` describes a position that will not exist, so it reports `size` `"0"`, `effectivePrice`, `oraclePrice`, `collateralReturned` and `debtRepaid` only: no leverage, liquidation price, buffer, health factor or borrow rate, because zeroes there would read as real, and `legs` is `[]`.

size.description: Exposure asset, native decimals, summed across legs. `"0"` on `close`.

leverage.description: Position over equity as a decimal string. Echoes the request's target on `open` and the six leverage-target keys, and is DERIVED from the position on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, where leverage follows from the collateral moving. Absent on `close`.

effectivePrice.description: The quoted fill including fees, impact and slippage, size-weighted across legs. A property of a swap, so it is absent on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which perform none: reporting the mark there would be the exact substitution this field exists to prevent. In TRADER terms (counter per exposure): on a short, the reciprocal of the operation's `effectivePrice`.

liquidationPrice.description: The oracle price at which LTV reaches LLTV. Multi-leg: the nearest leg's, because legs liquidate independently. Absent on `close`. In TRADER terms (counter per exposure), the same frame as `oraclePrice` and `effectivePrice`.

healthFactor.description: collateral x LLTV / debt; liquidatable below 1, that is below `"1000000000000000000"`. Nearest leg. The one risk number that normalizes across venues, so it is what a client bands into Healthy / Caution / Risky; the band thresholds are a product call and stay client-side. Absent on `close`.

borrowRate.description: Annualized borrow rate on the debt, size-weighted across legs. Absent when the selected venue's rate read supplied none, and on `close`.

oraclePrice.description: The venue's liquidation-reference price, in TRADER terms (counter per exposure): reciprocated on a short, the same frame as `effectivePrice` and `liquidationPrice`.

collateralReturned.description: `close` only: the collateral handed back after the router has sold what `maxCollateralIn` allows to buy the debt back. The floor of the payout, since the cap is padded against the caller.

debtRepaid.description: `close` only: the debt the position owed as read, which is what the close clears. Smaller than the operation's `debtToRepay`, whose excess the `SWEEP` returns.

MarginEquityAction.description:
`addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`. Size is held and leverage follows, so no leverage target.

`amount` is denominated in `walletToken` on `addEquity` and in the COLLATERAL token on `withdrawEquity`. That asymmetry is deliberate: how much collateral can leave before health hits the floor is answerable from the position alone, so denominating a withdrawal in `walletToken` would make whether it is allowed move with the funding route. It also matches the on-chain primitive, which takes a collateral amount.

MarginEquityLeverageAction.description: The four composites. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried.

amount.description: The equity magnitude, in `walletToken`'s native decimals.

MarginExecution.description: Everything `POST /plan` needs, and nothing it does not. This subtree is what a client echoes back to create a plan; `display` never is.

direction.description: Echoed from the request. Always present, including at its default `LONG`.

intent.description: Which action was priced, derived from the request's action key. Always present.

leverageTarget.description: Echoed from the request. Present iff the action key names a leverage target: `open` and the six leverage-target keys. Absent on `close`, `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`.

slippageTolerance.description: The leverage leg's confirmed tolerance, echoed from the top-level `slippageTolerance`. Absent on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which forbid it because they price no leverage leg. There is no AMM allowlist beside it: the leverage leg is v4 by construction, so it could not honour one; the wallet-side swap carries its own in the request's `swapConfig.protocols`.

funding.description: The wallet-side swap as priced. Present IFF a swap was actually priced, so its presence is the signal that one happened. Absent when the action moves no equity in (`close`, `increaseLeverage`, `decreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquity` and the two withdraw composites), and absent when `walletToken` already IS the position's collateral, since paying in the collateral itself needs no swap and a block whose input and output name the same token and amount describes no trade.

legs.description: Always present. One entry today: a single venue carries the whole position.

MarginExecutionLeg.description: One venue's share of the action, as an ordered list of on-chain operations. One venue carries the whole position today, so `legs` has exactly one entry.

venue.description: The lending venue this leg routes to. Always present, including at its default `MORPHO`.

subId.description: Server-resolved on the manage keys, where it is the `positionId` the request addressed. Absent on `open` until plan create allocates one.

operations.description: Ordered, in the sequence they execute. One on the simple keys. A composite populates more than one, with the equity side on opposite ends depending on which way it moves: a supply (`ADD_COLLATERAL`) goes FIRST, because it strictly lowers LTV, and a withdrawal (`WITHDRAW`) goes LAST, matching what the router does. `close` is a `DECREASE_POSITION` followed by a `SWEEP`.

MarginFunding.description: The wallet-side swap as priced, in the same shape `/quote` uses for an ordinary swap, so the funding leg reads natively rather than inventing a fourth swap-quote vocabulary. Present IFF a swap was actually priced, so its presence is the signal that one happened. `output.minimumAmount` is the equity the position was SIZED on, not `output.amount`: collateral the swap does not deliver is collateral the venue never receives. Carries no `protocols` and no `autoSlippage`: the first was a request echo that no consumer read and that could not express absence, and the second is a request-side mode whose only useful answer is the percent it resolved to, which `slippageTolerance` already carries.

tokenInChainId.description: Where `walletToken` sits. Equal to `tokenOutChainId` today, since cross-chain funding is not served.

input.description: The caller's spend in `walletToken`. Exact-in, so `maximumAmount` equals `amount`.

output.description: The collateral bought. `minimumAmount` is the floor the position is sized against; `recipient` is the `swapper`.

slippageTolerance.description: The wallet-side tolerance the floor was derived at, which `POST /plan` re-derives against. Echoed from `swapConfig.slippageTolerance`, which is required in practice today since `autoSlippage` is not resolved yet.

minBridgeOut.description: Cross-chain pay-in only: the guaranteed bridge floor. Not populated today, since cross-chain funding is refused with `MARGIN_FUNDING_SWAP_UNSUPPORTED`.

priceImpact.description: How far this swap lands from the pool's price, as a percent, exactly as `/quote` reports it. Reported, never refused: this leg spends the caller's own funds at the tolerance they chose, unlike the leverage leg, whose impact is multiplied by leverage and is refused past a ceiling with a 422 `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT`. Absent when the quote carried no measurement, which is not the same as zero.

MarginIntent.description: The action that was priced, carried as the proto enum's full member name (`MARGIN_INTENT_OPEN`, not `OPEN`). Mirrors the request's action key one to one, so a client can tell what it got without re-deriving it from its own request, and matches the vocabulary of the `MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH` error and the plan steps. Always present, including at its default `MARGIN_INTENT_OPEN`.

MarginLeverageAction.description: `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`. Equity is held, so no amount.

MarginLeverageLeg.description: The LEVERAGE leg's controls: the flash-accounted, debt-funded swap inside the router. Required on every action that moves leverage, and forbidden on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which hold size and let leverage follow.

slippageTolerance.description: The leverage leg's tolerance, always an explicit percentage. Independent of `swapConfig.slippageTolerance`; neither defaults from the other. There is deliberately no `autoSlippage` counterpart here, because this tolerance derives `maxDebtIn`/`maxCollateralIn`, which stamp into calldata as the MEV backstop, and a routing heuristic must not size a binding fund-safety bound.

MarginMarketRow.description: One row per (exposureToken, counterToken, direction). A venue market is a (collateral, debt) pair, and each one produces BOTH readings: the same on-chain position is a long of its collateral and a short of its debt, and shorting a token is only ever expressible as a market whose debt it is. Carries no `oraclePrice`: a mark belongs to a VENUE's oracle and two venues on one market need not agree, so a row-level price is a number no venue necessarily quoted. Carries no `feeBps` either: a pool fee tier is not a cost, since a 5bps pool with thin liquidity fills worse than a 30bps pool with depth. `effectivePrice` on a quote answers that, carrying the fee and the impact together.

MarginMarketVenue.description: What one venue offers for a pair, for the advanced breakdown. The scalars beside `venues` on the row are the HEADLINE venue's; read `headlineVenue` rather than matching them back.

venueMarketId.description: Morpho's market id. Absent where the (adapter, pair) IS the market.

maxLeverage.description: Decimal string, derived from the venue's BORROW-side LTV with the LTV cliff buffer already applied. Server-authored: a client must not compute this from `lltv`, or its ceiling and the quote's refusal disagree. The policy ceiling, not a guarantee: a quote near it can still be refused once its swap is priced. Note the buffer SCALES the ceiling rather than subtracting from it, so 86% at 400bps is 82.56% and not 82%.

lltv.description: The liquidation boundary itself, 18-decimal fixed point. Shown, never used to derive the ceiling.

borrowRate.description: Annual borrow rate, 18-decimal fixed point. Read from chain through the same function `POST /margin/quote` reads it through, so the venue a picker recommends is the venue a quote would pick for the same reason. Absent when the venue's rate read failed, which is not a rate of zero.

availableBorrowLiquidity.description: What the venue can actually lend, in raw debt-token units. On Aave this is `min(virtual balance, borrow cap - debt)`: the cap usually binds first, so the balance alone overstates it. Absent when the read failed, and always absent on `AAVE_V4`, whose liquidity is not read.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page, which is how a client knows to stop. Present means more rows exist, never that the next page is non-empty.

MarginMarketsResponse.description: A page of markets. Rows are in a total order over (exposureToken, counterToken, direction), so a token's rows are contiguous and a cursor resolves to the same row across a catalogue rebuild.

MarginOpenAction.description: `open`. No `positionId`: the server allocates one at plan create.

amount.description: The equity magnitude, in `walletToken`'s native decimals.

MarginOperation.description: The confirmed bounds for one operation. Which fields are set follows from `type`; they are the numbers that stamp into router calldata, so token amounts are in the token's native decimals while LTV and prices are 18-decimal fixed point.

type.description: Which on-chain router call this operation compiles to. Always present.

collateralToBuy.description: `INCREASE_POSITION` only: the exact-out buy of the collateral asset.

maxDebtIn.description: `INCREASE_POSITION` only: the binding cap on debt spent, the expected debt padded UP by the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance`. Mandatory and non-zero on-chain, since the router refuses a zero bound outright; a fill too small to bound is refused as a 422 `MARGIN_SWAP_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`. Derived from the top-level tolerance and never from `swapConfig`'s, so widening the wallet-side swap cannot loosen the MEV backstop.

debtToRepay.description: `DECREASE_POSITION` only: the debt cleared at the venue. On `close` this deliberately EXCEEDS the debt read at quote time by the projected accrual over the inclusion window, so the repay does not come up short and revert; the trailing `SWEEP` returns the excess.

maxCollateralIn.description: `DECREASE_POSITION` only: the cap on collateral sold to raise `debtToRepay`, padded UP by the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance`.

maxLtvAfter.description: The health assertion the router checks AFTER executing, so the calldata enforces the ceiling the quote refused to cross rather than trusting the fill to respect it. Set on every operation of the equity keys and the six leverage-target keys; absent on `open`, on `close` and on `SWEEP`.

amount.description: `ADD_COLLATERAL` and `WITHDRAW` only: the magnitude in the collateral token, always positive, since the direction is the operation's own. On an add that was funded by a wallet-side swap this is the swap's FLOOR (`funding.output.minimumAmount`) rather than its expected output, because collateral the swap does not deliver is collateral the venue never receives.

minHopPrice.description: Optional per-hop bound; `"0"` disables it. 18-decimal on the wire, X36 at encode. Not populated today.

effectivePrice.description: This operation's quoted fill, and the price-drift reference when `POST /plan` re-stamps. On the venue's own (collateral, debt) orientation, debt per collateral, so a short's reads inverted relative to `display.effectivePrice`. Present on `INCREASE_POSITION` and `DECREASE_POSITION`, the two operations that swap; absent on the rest.

MarginOperationType.description: One on-chain call inside the router's `execute([...actions])` stream. Which fields of the operation are set follows from this type. `INCREASE_POSITION` buys collateral with borrowed debt; `DECREASE_POSITION` sells collateral to repay debt; `ADD_COLLATERAL` and `WITHDRAW` move collateral across the wallet boundary without swapping; `SWEEP` carries no fields and returns whatever a `close`'s deliberate debt over-buy did not need, so the dust is not stranded in a position the caller believes is gone.

MarginPendingPlan.description: The one plan-store read, and a deliberately weaker guarantee than the rest of this response: session-scoped and TTL-bound, so absent rather than wrong once a row ages out. Acceptable only because no funds are at risk in that state.

createdAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. Rendered as a string by proto3 JSON; the client does not sort on it.

currentStep.description: 0-based index of the first step that is not COMPLETE.

cancellable.description: False once an in-progress step carries a proof: that transaction may have landed, so cancelling could strand what it moved.

MarginPositionAction.description: `close`. The whole position, so structurally neither a leverage target nor an amount.

MarginPositionLeg.description: One venue's share of a position. Legs liquidate independently, which is why the row's risk numbers are the nearest leg's rather than a blend.

subId.description: The `positionId` handle every quote action key echoes back. Returned whether or not a screen renders it.

account.description: The MarginAccount this leg lives at, derived offchain from (swapper, subId).

borrowRate.description: Best effort, like the markets feed: absent when the venue's rate read did not return, never zero, because an unread rate and a zero rate differ.

MarginPositionRow.description: One logical position, keyed on (exposureToken, counterToken, direction) — the same key the markets cursor orders on, which is why both endpoints page identically. Balances add across legs; risk does not.

size.description: Exposure held, in exposure-token base units.

entryPrice.description: Cost basis. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

openedAt.description: Cost basis. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

accruedInterest.description: Cost basis. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

unrealizedPnl.description: Cost basis. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

roe.description: Cost basis. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

equity.description: Collateral net of debt, each leg's debt valued at its own venue mark, in COLLATERAL-token base units: the exposure token on a LONG, the counter token on a SHORT, so scale it by that token's decimals. Absent when a leg's mark could not be read.

leverage.description: Collateral over equity, as a decimal string (`"1.83"`): the encoding `POST /margin/quote` serves as `display.leverage` and reads back as a leverage target, never a raw WAD integer. Absent when the position is underwater: with no equity there is no finite leverage, and `healthFactor` is below 1e18.

oraclePrice.description: The nearest leg's VENUE mark, in trader terms. This is the price risk is measured against, and it is not the price a swap would fill at.

liquidationPrice.description: Nearest leg, in trader terms. `oraclePrice / liquidationPrice` equals `healthFactor` on a LONG; on a SHORT, where both prices are reciprocated, `liquidationPrice / oraclePrice` does.

buffer.description: How far the mark can move before the nearest leg liquidates, as a WAD fraction of the mark. Zero at or past liquidation, never negative: `healthFactor` says how far past.

borrowRate.description: Debt-weighted across legs that reported one. Legs whose rate read failed are excluded rather than counted as zero.

maxWithdrawable.description: Collateral that can be withdrawn while staying under the BUFFERED ceiling. There is no on-chain guard on a withdraw, so this figure is the whole guard — do not recompute it from `lltv`.

closedAt.description: Terminal only. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

exitPrice.description: Terminal only. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

realizedPnl.description: Terminal only. Absent in v1 pending the margin event consumer.

MarginPositionStatus.description: Only `ACTIVE` is served today. The walk finds positions that still exist, so a terminal row has to come from events rather than from the chain's current state.

MarginPositionsResponse.description: A page of positions. Rows are in a total order over (exposureToken, counterToken, direction), the same order the markets feed uses.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page, which is how a client knows to stop. Present means more rows exist, never that the next page is non-empty.

pendingPlans.description: The margin plans this swapper started and has not finished, newest first, so a client can offer to resume or cancel one. Terminal plans are excluded server-side, and so is a plan whose execute deadline has passed, since its MARGIN_EXECUTE can only revert; one with an in-progress step carrying a proof stays, uncancellable, because that transaction may have landed. Served on the first page only: a request carrying `cursor` gets [] here, so concatenating pages never repeats a plan. Serializes as [] when the read ran and found nothing; it cannot express "not read", so a degraded plan-store read logs a warning and reports empty rather than failing the page.

MarginProtocols.description: The AMM allowlist for the swap legs, distinct from `venues`, which is the lending allowlist. Only Uniswap AMM protocols are eligible: a margin leg is flash-accounted inside the router, so UniswapX order types cannot serve it.

MarginQuoteAddEquityAndDecreaseLeverageR.description: Add equity and lower leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteAddEquityAndIncreaseLeverageR.description: Add equity and raise leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteAddEquityRequest.description: Add equity and let leverage fall. Size is held, so there is no leverage swap to bound. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage is not targeted, so the top-level `slippageTolerance` is forbidden. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteCloseRequest.description: Close the whole position. Structurally neither a leverage target nor an amount: it is the entire position. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteDecreaseLeverageRequest.description: Lower leverage on an existing position. Equity is held, so nothing crosses the wallet boundary. `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are forbidden. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteIncreaseLeverageRequest.description: Raise leverage on an existing position. Equity is held, so nothing crosses the wallet boundary. `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are forbidden. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteOpenRequest.description: Open a new position. The server allocates the position id at plan create, so no `positionId` is sent. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteRequest.description:
Prices one margin action. The request is the shared block plus EXACTLY ONE of the ten action keys: `open`, `close`, `increaseLeverage`, `decreaseLeverage`, `addEquity`, `withdrawEquity`, `addEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `addEquityAndDecreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquityAndDecreaseLeverage`. Sending none of them, or more than one, is rejected: both are structural, not field-presence rules applied after the fact.

Every field inside an action key is required, so what a caller must send follows entirely from which action it is doing. There are no optional fields inside a key and no field whose absence carries meaning.

Two shared blocks are required-or-forbidden per key, never optional. The wallet block (`walletToken`, `walletChainId`, `swapConfig`) is forbidden on `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`, which hold equity, and required on the other eight. The top-level `slippageTolerance`, the leverage leg's, is forbidden on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which hold size, and required on the other eight. Each variant below states its own rule.

Amounts are decimal strings in the token's native decimals. Leverage is a decimal string. Prices, the liquidation health factors and borrow rates are unsuffixed 18-decimal fixed point.

Unknown fields are rejected with a 400 rather than ignored, so a retired or misspelled field fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing. This cannot be stated in the schema itself: the variants compose their shared blocks with `allOf`, and `additionalProperties: false` under `allOf` would reject the very fields the sibling blocks contribute.

MarginQuoteRequestBase.description: The fields every margin action sends, whichever action key it uses. Never sent on its own: a request is one of the ten `MarginQuote*Request` variants, each of which is this block plus its action key and that key's required peers.

positionChainId.description: The chain the POSITION lives on. Named rather than left as a bare `chainId` because two chains are in play: with one of them unqualified a client reasonably reads it as "the" chain, sets it to the chain it is paying from, and silently gets a cross-chain funding flow it never asked for.

exposureToken.description: The token the position is exposed to. Which side of the market this is depends on `direction`, never on the order of the pair.

counterToken.description: The other side of the market. Which side of the market this is depends on `direction`, never on the order of the pair.

MarginQuoteResponse.description:
A priced margin action. `execution` is what `POST /plan` consumes; `display` is what the confirmation modal renders and is ignored by `/plan`.

Every enum field is serialized, including at its protobuf default value, so an absent enum never has to be read as a default, and every `repeated` field is serialized, as `[]` when empty. `optional` fields are absent when unset.

gasEstimate.description: Indicative gas estimate for the resulting plan, and INDICATIVE is the operative word: the transaction does not exist at quote time, so there is no calldata to estimate against. Exactly one of `eip1559` and `legacy` is set. `gasLimit` is a per-intent measured fallback rather than a per-request estimate; `maxFeePerGas` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas` are live network readings. No `strategy` is served: the fee comes from an urgency path that returns none, so any strategy shown would describe an algorithm that did not run. Absent entirely when the gas oracle is unavailable, which does not fail the quote.

MarginQuoteWithdrawEquityAndDecreaseLeve.description: Withdraw equity and lower leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteWithdrawEquityAndIncreaseLeve.description: Withdraw equity and raise leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteWithdrawEquityRequest.description: Withdraw equity and let leverage rise. Size is held, so there is no leverage swap to bound. `amount` here is denominated in the COLLATERAL token, not `walletToken`; the one place the "amount is always walletToken" rule breaks. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage is not targeted, so the top-level `slippageTolerance` is forbidden. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginSwapConfig.description:
Execution policy for the WALLET-side swap, and nothing else. It names no token, no chain, no amount and no trade type: identity lives at the top level in `walletToken`/`walletChainId`, the magnitude lives in the action key, and exact-in versus exact-out follows from whether the action pays in or pays out.

`slippageTolerance` is required and must be below 100, since at 100% the floor the position is sized on is zero. `autoSlippage` is refused by name with a `RequestValidationError`, as on the leverage leg: this tolerance derives that floor, and a resolved auto-slippage value is not visible to the sizing path.

Kept separate from `walletToken` because the two have different lifetimes: `walletToken` is always meaningful, while this block can be moot, since paying in the collateral token needs no funding swap at all and whether one is needed is a routing outcome not knowable at request time.

slippageTolerance.description: The WALLET-side swap’s tolerance, from 0 up to but excluding 100. Derives `funding.output.minimumAmount`, which is the equity the position is sized on — not `funding.output.amount`.

routingPreference.description: Defaults to `BEST_PRICE`, matching every other quote in this API. This leg is the slowest call in a margin quote, and `FASTEST` takes roughly a second off it for a handful of basis points -- which `slippageTolerance` already floors before the position is sized. Send `FASTEST` when the quote is indicative and the latency matters more than the last few bps.

MarginTokenMetadata.description: A token as a response carries it. No symbol or name: this endpoint resolves markets, not token metadata, and a client merges display fields from its own token lists by address.

MarginVenue.description: A lending venue the position can be held at.

MarginVenues.description: The LENDING allowlist for the position, distinct from `protocols`, which is the AMM allowlist for the swap legs. At least one venue must be named; the server ranks the allowed venues and serves the best one.

MarginWalletBlock.description: The wallet-side block: the token crossing the wallet boundary, where it sits, and how its swap should execute. Required in full on every action that moves equity, and forbidden in full on `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`, which hold equity. It is never genuinely optional: whether it applies follows from the action key alone.

walletToken.description: The token crossing the wallet boundary. Deliberately not named `tokenIn`: `close` and the `withdrawEquity*` keys pay OUT, so an "in" name would be wrong on four of the ten keys. Flow direction is read off the action key and never restated here. The action key's `amount` is denominated in this token, except on `withdrawEquity`.

walletChainId.description: Where `walletToken` sits. Differing from `positionChainId` means cross-chain funding, which is pay-in only.

marginFixedPoint18.description: An unsuffixed 18-decimal fixed-point value as an integer string: divide by 10^18 to read it. Prices, the liquidation buffer, health factors, borrow rates, LTVs and equity shares all use this scale regardless of the tokens' own decimals. Every field on this scale is non-negative, `buffer` included: it is a distance to liquidation, not a signed move.

marginLeverage.description: Leverage as a decimal string (`"3"`, `"2.55"`), never a number. Leverage is money-adjacent, so it is carried as a string to keep it out of float rounding. Must be greater than 1: leverage buys collateral with borrowed funds, so 1x buys nothing and opens no position. Rejected at the boundary rather than deep in sizing.

marginPositionId.description: The id of an existing margin position, as a decimal integer string with no leading zeros, at most 2^256 - 1 (the router's uint256 subId). Absent on `open`, where the server allocates it at plan create.

universalRouterVersionHeader.name: x-universal-router-version
universalRouterVersionHeader.description: The version of the Universal Router to use for the swap journey. *MUST* be consistent throughout the API calls.

erc20EthEnabledHeader.name: x-erc20eth-enabled
erc20EthEnabledHeader.description: Enable native ETH input support for UniswapX via ERC20-ETH (EIP-7914). When set to true and `tokenIn` is the native currency address (e.g. `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), the API may return UniswapX routes that spend native ETH for supported wallets.

permit2DisabledHeader.name: x-permit2-disabled
permit2DisabledHeader.description: Disables the Permit2 approval flow. When set to `true`, `permitData` is returned as `null` and the header is forwarded to the routing layer for correct gas simulation against the Proxy Universal Router contract. When `false` or omitted, the standard Permit2 approval flow is used. This header is intended for integrators whose infrastructure uses a direct approval-then-swap pattern without Permit2.

swapStepsEnabledHeader.name: x-universal-router-swapsteps
swapStepsEnabledHeader.description: Opts the request into Universal Router swap steps mode. Required for Guidestar routing, together with `x-api-experimental`. When Guidestar routes the quote, the `CLASSIC` quote includes a `swapSteps` array describing the Universal Router swap sequence. Omitting the header or setting it to `false` keeps the standard response shape.

experimentalRoutingHeader.name: x-api-experimental
experimentalRoutingHeader.description: Requests Guidestar routing. Requires `x-universal-router-swapsteps: true`. Supported for `EXACT_INPUT` quotes on Ethereum (1), Base (8453), and Robinhood Chain (4663); any other request, including one without the swap steps header, returns a 400 `InputValidationError`. A Guidestar request does not fall back to standard routing: if Guidestar cannot produce a quote, the request returns a 404. Guidestar routing is in beta and its behavior may change. Omitting the header or setting it to `false` keeps standard routing.

agentInfoHeader.name: x-agent-info
agentInfoHeader.description: Optional attribution hint for AI-agent traffic; send it if an AI agent built or operates your integration. The value is a JSON object with up to three fields: `decision_origin` (required, exactly `autonomous` or `human_mediated`, case-sensitive), `integration_name` (optional string naming your integration, e.g. `my-trading-bot`), and `version` (optional string identifying your integration's version). Any other key is dropped, never rejected. The raw value must be at most 1024 bytes of printable US-ASCII (`0x20`-`0x7E`), so send non-ASCII text as JSON `\u` escapes; `integration_name` and `version` are each limited to 256 UTF-16 code units and may not contain control characters, U+2028, U+2029, or U+FFFD. Send the header once: repeated header lines are joined with `, ` and the joined string is what gets parsed, so two complete objects fail as invalid JSON while a single object split across two lines still parses. The header is analytics-only and never affects the request: omitting it, sending it, or sending a value that fails these rules never changes the response status, body, or swap behavior. A value that fails to parse is dropped and reported by the `x-agent-info-status` response header. Never put a user ID, wallet address, email, session token, or API key in these fields.

orderTypeParam.name: orderType
orderTypeParam.description: The UniswapX order type to retrieve.

orderIdParam.name: orderId
orderIdParam.description: A transaction hash for an order. `orderId` or `orderIds` must be provided, but not both.

orderIdsParam.name: orderIds
orderIdsParam.description: A list of comma separated orderIds (transaction hashes). `orderId` or `orderIds` must be provided, but not both.

sortKeyParam.name: sortKey
sortKeyParam.description: Order the query results by the sort key.

transactionHashesParam.description: On-chain transaction hashes. At least one of `txHashes` or `userOpHashes` must be provided.
transactionHashesParam.name: txHashes

userOpHashesParam.description: ERC-4337 UserOperation hashes. At least one of `txHashes` or `userOpHashes` must be provided.
userOpHashesParam.name: userOpHashes

tokenListLimitParam.name: limit
tokenListLimitParam.description: Number of ranked tokens to return. Applies only when sort is `tvl` or `volume_24h`. Defaults to 100.

tokenListChainIdParam.name: chainId
tokenListChainIdParam.description: Filter ranked token results to a specific chain. When omitted, ranked results include all supported chains. Ignored when sort is `default`.

agentInfoStatusHeader.description: Present, with the fixed value `malformed`, only when the request carried an `x-agent-info` header that failed to parse and was dropped; the value never echoes anything from the request. Absent when `x-agent-info` parsed, was not sent, or was sent with an empty value, which the gateway treats as not sent. Set by the API gateway once it has resolved the route and before it proxies the request, so it is returned on every response, including gateway-generated errors such as 400, 401, 403, and 429. It reports attribution only; the request itself succeeds or fails independently of it.
